skills.title: Clean-then-place with verified cleaning
skills.principle: For a goal requiring a clean object to be placed, use separate stages: locate and acquire the named target; bring it to a compatible cleaning fixture, preferring a sinkbasin; clean it; verify from the observation that cleaning succeeded; then go to the destination, open it if closed, and place the object. Do not place before cleaning, and do not treat cleaning as complete without confirming evidence. If cleaning did not succeed, return to the cleaning stage before placement. If a transfer or handoff occurs after acquisition, record that cleaning is still required. Treat successful placement as the terminal condition.
skills.when_to_apply: When the goal is to put a clean object in or on a specified receptacle and the object is not already clean.

skills.title: Cleaning no-effect: verify position, held object, fixture, and cleanability
skills.description: A cleaning action may produce no effect when the target is not held, the actor is not actually at a valid cleaning fixture, the current location is not a cleaning fixture, or the object is unsuitable. A sinkbasin is reliably supported in observations; alternatives such as a bathtubbasin or fridge should not be assumed equivalent. Some objects, such as towels or cloth, may not support cleaning at a sinkbasin, and repeated attempts can keep failing. Repeating identical cleaning attempts wastes steps, and trying to take another object while still holding a failed object may also produce repeated no-ops.
skills.why_it_happens: The environment appears to validate that the target is held, that cleaning occurs at a compatible fixture, and that the object is cleanable; naming a fixture in a command does not substitute for being at it. Not every fixture or object supports cleaning.
skills.how_to_avoid: Hold the target and be at a sinkbasin before cleaning. If there is no effect, first verify that the actor is actually at the sinkbasin, then verify the held object and current location; try a different sinkbasin or confirm the object is cleanable. Treat a bathtubbasin as unverified and switch to a sinkbasin if cleaning fails. If the object type is likely non-cleanable, stop repeating cleaning; release it at a valid surface before trying another candidate, then try another cleanable candidate or report that the object is not cleanable. Do not loop on the same action.

skills.title: Placement failure: open, verify capacity, and avoid invalid destinations
skills.description: Placement can fail when the destination container is closed, has no available space, or is not a valid receptacle. Some fixtures, such as toilets or coffeemachines, may reject placement, and repeated put/open/use attempts on a coffeemachine can return no effect. An open action may also return no effect when the container is already open or not openable.
skills.why_it_happens: Containers may require opening or have capacity limits, and some fixtures are not valid placement targets. Repeating put or open without changing conditions can waste steps.
skills.how_to_avoid: Before placing, open a closed destination. If open returns no effect, do not retry it; treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed or reassess. Check space or availability when possible. If the destination is invalid or placement repeatedly has no effect, seek an alternative valid destination or report blocked rather than looping.

skills.title: Use the specified object type; do not silently substitute
skills.description: Goals specify an object type. Similar alternatives such as a mug for a cup, a pan for a pot, or a butterknife for a knife should not be silently substituted. A close synonym may be used only if the exact object is unavailable and the environment or observation explicitly treats it as equivalent, or the goal permits it; otherwise continue searching or report the mismatch. If the destination already contains a similar object, still acquire, clean, and place the correct target rather than swapping.
skills.why_it_happens: Generalizing categories can cause taking the wrong item and failing the task, while exact-name matching may miss an accepted synonym. Equivalence must be confirmed rather than assumed.
skills.how_to_avoid: Search first for the exact named type. If it is not found, do not swap in a different type by default; use only a confirmed equivalent. Confirm equivalence through explicit environmental or observational evidence or goal permission before substituting.

skills.title: Prioritized search with bounded backtracking
skills.description: Search should prioritize plausible locations but avoid opening every remaining container indefinitely or declaring blocked prematurely. Track checked locations and avoid revisiting confirmed-empty ones. After a reasonable set of likely locations has been checked—not merely one or two when many plausible ones remain—consider unusual placement or impossibility, then reassess or report blocked. Open surfaces such as stoveburners, countertops, and dining tables must be included, not only cabinets and drawers.
skills.why_it_happens: Item locations may follow regularities, but unusual placement or impossible tasks can occur. Unbounded search wastes steps and can cause timeout, while stopping too early can miss findable objects. Restricting search to closed containers misses objects placed on open surfaces.
skills.how_to_avoid: Prioritize likely locations by object type: food-related items in a fridge; dishes or utensils on a countertop, in a cabinet, or in a drawer; pots, kettles, or pans on stoveburners; cleaning supplies near a sinkbasin, countertop, or shelf. Keep a record of checked locations. After several likely locations fail, consider unusual placement or impossibility and reassess or report blocked rather than exhaustively opening all containers or stopping after only a couple of empty locations.
